summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the confidential launch data, find where the Sunday 20:00 launch actually breaks, and build a general recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, supplier emails with approval) plus its UI.
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's plan says all ok while the Collector's Edition misses launch (overbooked art books, failed statues, packing speed, game cards short). Built a working app (versioned poller, verifier, case cards, email send/reply tracking, routines, drop-handling fixes) and sent the Karton Nowak art-book order. Remaining work: push, README, demo script and video before the 12:00 hand-in.

repo: Portal API has only GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip, with no webhooks or change feed. Files are replaced under the same name, so change detection must compare per-file SHA-256 checksums.
Confidential challenge data lives in gitignored data/ (raw, drops, notes, img); .env is gitignored and .env.example is committed.
Team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md (claim tasks with a Now line). Work is on branch jonas/today-flow with many unpushed commits.

The mailbox is shared by the app, manual sends and Lucas's Pulse tool. The app was blind to non-app sends, which caused a double order to Karton, so outbox.py now syncs the sent folder and guards duplicate sends (409 unless 'Send anyway').
Routines and the spoken 'yes' all go through the same approve function, so a guard there covers every send path.
Side-email replies logged on a case used to mark it 'sent' and drop it from 'Needs you'. A reply should add information only, not decide the case.
Entire hooks only checkpoint when repo files change; sessions with no repo changes log 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint'.
The app routes every costed case to Maren, but the policy gives Paul Winter 50k EUR buyer authority, so limits should come from the policy.

code.finding: New module that reads the shared mailbox's sent folder and assigns emails to cases by thread reference, then supplier plus PO, then a part number unique to one case.

Compares newer supplier profile JSON with profile.csv to raise status and qualification cards. A new contact email is only used as a send target after explicit confirmation. Commit b0cff82 accidentally imported it before it was tracked.
Delay notices with a new date now count as late. It no longer auto-resolves cards when an input it used to read is unreadable (tracked in papercheck_reads.json).

Routine diagram rewritten as When, a single Only if node (AND list with funnel counts), and one node per Then step. Funnel counts are computed in the browser and mirror routines.py, so they can drift.
Case list in the left column now expands, is sticky and self-scrolling. No row in 'Needs you' is marked selected while a decided case is open, which was what made the list jump to the top.

workflow: A drop drill on a copy of the data (second server, background loops off, LLM off) safely exercises new-file scenarios without touching real mail or portal.
Use subagents for bulk cross-checks (200 order confirmations plus 59 scans) and for UX review and redesign; verify results with screenshots before committing.
Commit in topic-sized commits and check that HEAD alone starts. Concurrent uncommitted work in a shared tree can leak into a commit.
Do not send supplier emails or push without explicit user approval.
Specific, data-grounded interview questions earn credibility, but the user preferred pain and product questions up front, split into General and Specific.

friction: Hackathon time pressure with a hand-in at 12:00 and many parallel threads.
The shared mailbox caused a double Karton order (06:50 via the app, 07:04 by hand) and Pulse sent three confusing test emails to Hwaseong.
Commit b0cff82 picked up uncommitted api.py edits that import an untracked module, so that commit alone would not start.
My manual tracking emails' replies closed three real cases (clear cases, statues, Boise) until I reopened them.
A UI bug put a stray period on its own line, because a button is a block element inside the sentence.
The chosen recommendation option had no key number or click target, so numbering started at 2.
A renamed stock column silently auto-resolved three real cards, and a news drop crashed the pipeline because two modules wrote impacts.json in different shapes.
A routine the user switched on had an option-matching bug, which I fixed and covered with a test.
It is unclear whether the portal data and drops are identical across teams.
open_items: Push the unpushed commits on jonas/today-flow (about 16); user approval pending.
Write the README, demo script and video for the 12:00 hand-in.
Combine the four 'Are there really…?' count questions into one case to cut the 17 cases in 'Needs you'.
Send the note to Hwaseong about the three Pulse test emails and draft a message to Lucas (Pulse has no allow-list). The bounced Gmail address leaked no data.
Finish the 'confirmed orders become inbound deliveries' builder: art books arrive about 19:30 but the cell runs dry at 11:16, so open a follow-up case for a van or split load.
Make the approval limits come from the policy, not everything with a cost to Maren.
Memo rules (Quality & Compliance last word, air/rush to CPO within the hour) are extracted but not yet used for routing.
The predictor with a real model is untested (it defaults to gpt-5 and costs money). Renamed columns are not guessed and the datacheck warning is the only signal.
Register sender addresses in the portal Settings, and consider rotating the portal password that was shared in Discord.
Share the briefing page with the team only. The older Claude doc duplicates it and could be deleted.
Codex hooks still need approval via /hooks.
